data.title: The Myth of AI Content
paragraphs: The pitch was clean. AI writes now. Point it at your blog, your product pages, and your emails, and the content problem goes away. Cancel the freelancer. Thin out the team. Let the machine run.

Then the content ships, and it reads like everyone else's. The writer you replaced did things their job description never listed. They knew your voice. They knew what was true. They had taste. They held context. Those skills never showed up on the invoice, and they were the whole point.

new_way.heading: The recipe that works

Ship content that sounds like you

data.title: What the myth costs you
data.subtitle: Remove the human and the failure modes are predictable. They show up the same way every time.

items.title: Everything sounds the same
items.text: Models drift toward the average of the internet. Your content starts to read like your competitor's, because both came from the same place.

items.title: Your voice drifts
items.text: A hedge here, a stock phrase there, a structure you would never have chosen. The brand reads like a brand, just not yours.

items.title: Specifics get fabricated
items.text: Statistics, quotes, and product details. A model will produce them whether or not they exist, and you find out which were invented when a customer does.

items.title: Your reach shrinks
items.text: Generic content does not rank, does not get cited by AI search, and does not get shared. You produced more and reached fewer.

data.title: The recipe, where the human stays in the loop
data.subtitle: Automate the drafting. Staff the judgment.

steps.title: Ideas
steps.text: Human-led. A person decides what your audience needs to hear. That comes from knowing the business.

steps.title: Research and outline
steps.text: Shared. AI gathers and structures. A person decides what matters and what the angle is.

steps.title: First draft
steps.text: AI-assisted. This is where the speed lives, and where a model earns its place.

steps.title: Editing and voice
steps.text: Human, always. Voice, cuts, point of view, the line that does not belong.

steps.title: Fact-checking
steps.text: Human, always. Every claim, number, and name verified by someone who can be held to it.

steps.title: Publish and strategy
steps.text: Human-led. What goes out, to whom, and how it connects to the pieces around it.

data.title: The review rubric
data.subtitle: Six checks a person runs on any AI draft before it ships. A model cannot run a single one.

items.title: Voice fidelity
items.text: Does this sound like us, not like content in general? If it could run on a competitor's site with the logo swapped, it fails.

items.title: Accuracy
items.text: Is every claim, number, name, and quote verified and true? No exceptions for the ones that sound right.

items.title: Originality
items.text: Is there a point of view here, or just a competent summary of what everyone already says?

items.title: Brand safety
items.text: Anything we would not want quoted back to us? A claim we cannot support, a tone that misreads the moment.

items.title: Strategic fit
items.text: Does this piece do a job, or just fill a slot on the calendar?

items.title: Sourcing
items.text: Can every fact in here be traced to something you could open and read? A claim with no source behind it is a guess wearing a confident sentence.

data.title: Human creativity, marketing intelligence
paragraphs: Content Cucumber is a human-powered marketing company. AI helps us draft faster. A person who already knows your brand keeps the voice yours.

The Content Flywheel Plan puts a dedicated writer and a content strategist behind your brand. A short monthly interview becomes a full month of content, sourced from what you said, so it sounds like you because it is you.

items.question: Is this anti-AI?
items.answer: No. We use AI where it helps, mostly in drafting and research. The point is keeping a person responsible for voice, facts, and judgment, the work a model cannot do.

items.question: Why pay for humans when AI is fast and cheap?
items.answer: Speed only helps if the content sounds like you and earns trust. A writer who knows your brand makes the review fast and the draft start closer to right, so you keep the speed without the sameness.

items.question: What is the Content Flywheel Plan?
items.answer: A short monthly interview with you becomes a full month of content. A dedicated writer and a content strategist handle production, and you pick the mix of blogs, social, and email.

items.question: Will AI-written content hurt my search rankings?
items.answer: Generic content does, whoever or whatever wrote it. Content with a real point of view and verified specifics is what ranks and what AI search cites. The rubric above is how we get there.
